svg.aria-label: Composer V2: chat-first agent authoring, five layers, one front door
svg.text: COMPOSER V2 — BUILD AN AGENT BY TALKING TO IT
V1 was a five-step stepper with typed form fields. It worked and nobody enjoyed it. V2 is a conversation — and did not build a second chat runtime.
THE PRINCIPLE — THREE LAYERS THAT NEVER BLUR
The USER speaks business intent
"Every Monday, tell me which customers slipped
on payment and what it costs us."
The LLM proposes structure
cadence · connectors · lookback · role lens
· customer scope · which capabilities to use
The SERVER owns the contract
Zod validation · materialisation · linting
· publish authority. Non-negotiable.
THE FOUR AUTHORING TOOLS — THE ONLY BRIDGE FROM CHAT TO THE AGENT PIPELINE
propose_agent_draft
Zod-validates the LLM's proposal against
ComposerIntentDraftV1 (business intent),
then MATERIALISES it into an
AgentDefinitionV1 and re-validates against
the same schema scheduled agents use.
validate_draft_silently
Runs the same 11-check linter the
publish path uses — not a lighter
"preview" variant.
Unknown capability names are rejected
at materialisation, not at run time.
dry_run_draft
Invokes the REAL MCP-backed agent
runtime with trigger:'dry-run'.
Not a simulation, not a preview render.
What you see in the chat is what the
scheduler will produce at 08:00.
PUBLISH
The LLM has no
publish tool.
A UI action carries a server-only
publishToken — generated, rotated
and consumed entirely server-side.
Draft store — deliberately ephemeral
· 30-minute TTL · identity-bound to the session
· deep-cloned on ingress AND egress, so no caller can mutate stored state by reference
· publishToken never appears in a model-visible tool result or a client payload · single-use after publish
What made this cheap to build
The chat engine already had multi-turn state, SSE streaming, tool execution, citation
extraction, auth context, telemetry, abort and retry — months of investment.
Composer V2 = same runtime + a different system prompt + a six-tool allowlist. That is the entire delta.
THE INVARIANT THAT MADE IT SAFE TO SHIP
V1-indistinguishability
Every agent published by Composer V2 must be byte-equivalent to one
authored through the old typed pipeline. A snapshot suite enforces it.
Which means: the scheduler, the runtime, the policy hooks and the
report format never had to learn that Composer V2 exists.
A new authoring UX shipped with zero blast radius on the execution path.
Twelve rounds of independent agent review are traced in the plan document.
NEXT — COMPOSER V3 (PLANNED)
V2's constraint: the artefact lives inside the chat. Iterating means
scrolling between the latest preview and the message you're refining.
V3 inverts it: the artefact is the viewport, chat becomes the side rail.
Plus three BI-specific affordances no general-purpose canvas has:
· lineage chip — which dataset produced this section
· plan-mode preview — see the tool plan before it runs
· per-section execution badges — what actually resolved, per block
